problem: Given the curve $r(t)=t\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})\,j \\  & =i-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ [t\,i+\frac{1}{t}\,j]\cdot (i-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\,j) & =0 \\ t\cdot 1-\frac{1}{t}\cdot \frac{1}{{t}^{2}} & =0 \\ t-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}} & =0 \\ {t}^{4} & =1 \\ t & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $t=\pm 1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1)=1\,i+\frac{1}{1}\,j=\,i+j, \\ r(-1)=(-1)\,i+\frac{1}{(-1)}\,j=-\,i-j,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the points $(1,1)$ and $(-1,-1).$
